column1: # quantities.tsv -- the declaration of WHAT EACH RUN MUST REPORT.
# matrix.tsv says WHAT TO RUN: 630 cells, each a procedure, a dataset and
# every option setting. It never said what a cell that ran must come back
# with. Without that, neither runner could be short of anything: a quantity
# absent from one table was indistinguishable from a feature the plugin does
# not have, and the difference was settled by writing a sentence in
# compare.R's DECLARED[] rather than by reading the plugin.
# That is how D-NOCI survived. It claimed no post-hoc comparison in the
# plugin returns a confidence interval, and it covered 1500 rows -- the
# largest entry in the table. @emlOneWayAnova returns .qCritical, .msWithin
# builds the family-wise half-width from exactly those three and PRINTS the
# interval, and the kit's own praat_reports/*.txt carry it:
#     -- Tukey HSD Mean Differences (95% family-wise CI) ---
# The Praat runner never read those bounds. With nothing declaring that a
# Tukey cell owes an interval, a runner bug looked like a plugin gap.
# DERIVED, NOT WRITTEN FROM MEMORY. Every row below was read off the source
# named in its `source` column, in this order of authority:
#   1. The procedure's own `Output:` / `Outputs:` header, where it has one.
#      CLAUDE.md requires reading that header before consuming a return,
#      precisely because the returned name differs from the parameter name.
#      (stats/eml-extract.praat:4370) -- THE WRITE SITE, the single place any
#      emlStore name is assigned. For the analysis lane this IS the
#      orchestrator's declared output surface: omnibus stat / df1 / df2 / p,
#      effect, n, the SECOND ARM where a door ran two tests of one
#      hypothesis, and the four post-hoc matrices
#   3. The reporter that prints it, where a quantity is assembled for the
#      report out of several kernel returns and has no single header of its
#      own (medians in the Group Descriptives block; the Tukey interval;
#      adjusted R-squared). A number a user reads in the Info window is a
#      number the plugin reports, whatever slot it arrives in.
# HEADERS READ: 32 procedures. The full list is in the `source` column;
# every distinct file:line there is a header that was opened and read.
# FINDING: 12 OF THE 13 ANALYSIS-LANE ORCHESTRATORS HAVE NO Outputs HEADER.
# stats/eml-analysis.praat is 4800 lines and contains exactly ONE `Outputs:`
# block (line 3193, @emlRunGroupedRegressionAnalysis) -- and that one lists only
# .pgTotal / .pgRun / .pgSkipped, the group counts, not one statistic. These
# They are the twelve doors a user actually walks through, and they are the
# twelve with nothing to read before consuming a return. That is why every
# analysis-lane row below cites either a KERNEL header (@emlTTest,
# @emlOneWayAnova, @emlKruskalWallis, ...) or the write site, never the
# orchestrator: the orchestrators do not say what they return, so the
# contract had to be assembled from the layer underneath them and from the
# layer above them. Recommend the twelve get headers; until they do, this
# file is the nearest thing to one, and it is in the wrong repository layer.
# Bookkeeping and disclosure fields that appear in the headers but are not
# results a reader states an outcome in: .error$, .warning$, .capped,
# .rowIndex#, .nPairs, .nGroups where a k is already contracted. Naming them
# here is the point: they are excluded on purpose, not overlooked.
# ADDED 26 August (post-hoc estimates/intervals work order, Items 2-5):
# nonparametric branch. Same shape as .method$ above: it discloses WHICH
# null distribution a pair's interval came from, not a result a reader
# states an outcome in. v145 reads it directly to check it agrees with the
# branch the pair's own p-value was computed on; it is not part of this
# contract for that reason, same as every other $-suffixed disclosure field.
# ADDED 27 August (item 22 of the language batch, Fable's ruling): p_method
# / spearman_p_method -- NOT an exception to the exclusion above, a
# graduation out of it. .method$ and .methodReason$ themselves stay
# excluded, same as ever (still bookkeeping, never printed on their own).
# What changed is that item 22 gave @emlMannWhitneyU, @emlWilcoxonSignedRank
# and @emlSpearmanCorrelationDispatch's composition of those two fields
# (plus Pearson's literal "t distribution") its own PRINTED report row --
# "p method", via the existing @emlReportLineString, always, never gated on
# emlShowExplanations. A number a user reads in the Info window is a number
# the plugin reports, whatever slot it arrives in (this file's own opening
# principle, above) -- so once item 22 made that composition a printed row,
# it is contracted like any other, not read directly off the two excluded
# fields the way v145 reads .hlMethod$ for its own internal cross-check.
# One header-listed RESULT is reported by neither runner and is named here so
# the gap is visible rather than absent: nothing else. @emlChiSquareIndependence's
# .nCellsBelow5 IS reported by both (n_cells_below5), and was the candidate.
#   procedure   the matrix.tsv procedure this contract clause governs
#   quantity    the quantity name in the shared long schema. Placeholders:
#                 <LEVEL> a group or condition level, slugged
#   scope       cell | pair | level | item | row | term -- how many of this
#               quantity one cell owes. `cell` owes exactly one.
#   when        the condition, over the cell's OWN AXES in matrix.tsv, under
#               which the cell owes it. Atoms: `always`; `<axis>=<value>`;
#               with `&`. A CONDITIONAL QUANTITY IS STILL CONTRACTED -- the
#               condition is written down, not used as an excuse to drop it.
#   sides       both | praat | r. `both` means each runner must report it and
#               the two are compared. `praat` / `r` means the quantity
#               belongs to that side alone, WITH THE REASON in `note` -- this
#               is the only thing that makes a one-sided row legitimate.
#   source      file:line of the header or reporter this row was read from.
#   note        why, where a `sides` other than `both` or a `when` other than
# HOW AN INDEX SET IS FIXED, and the one place this file reads output.
# `cell`- and `term`-scoped quantities are expanded from the declaration
# alone: one per cell, and for `term` the three two-way terms built from
# col_b, col_c and their interaction. `level`-scoped quantities on the
# repeated-measures and Friedman rows likewise come from the declaration --
# matrix.tsv's col_a IS the pipe-delimited condition list. But the group
# labels behind <PAIR>, the surviving <ROW> numbers and the <ITEM> columns
# are properties of the DATA, not of the declaration, and deriving them here
# would mean re-implementing each runner's row filtering in a third place.
# For those, compare.R takes the index set as the UNION of the indices each
# side actually emitted for that cell. That is weaker than a declaration and
# it is stated plainly rather than hidden: it cannot catch a pair BOTH
# runners drop, but it catches every case where one side reports an index and
# the other does not -- which is the entire class of defect this file exists
# A quantity counts as REPORTED if the side emitted `<quantity>` or
# `<quantity>_undefined`. A runner that says "this is undefined here" has
# reported it; a runner that writes no row has not. That convention is the
# kit's first documented DELIBERATE divergence between the plugin and R on a
# quantity both sides compute the same way in principle.
# The Hodges-Lehmann shift estimate is DEFINED as the median of the
# cross-differences (two-sample) or the median of the Walsh averages
# (paired). On the exact branch R's own `$estimate` IS that median. On the
# NORMAL-APPROXIMATION branch, R's `$estimate` is instead whatever
# `uniroot()` returns for its confidence-curve inversion -- an artefact of
# that root-finding shortcut, measured about 4e-5 away from R's OWN
# exact-branch answer on the same data (v145 asserts this: R disagrees with
# itself across its two branches on the one number both branches call by the
# THE RULE: where the published definition and R's implementation diverge,
# the plugin follows the DEFINITION, not the implementation, and the kit
# oracles the plugin's estimate against `median(outer(x, y, "-"))` (or the
# Walsh-average equivalent) rather than against R's `$estimate` on the
# approximation branch -- reporting R's value alongside, never silently. The
# interval BOUNDS are exempted from this rule and still port R's
# continuity-corrected inversion verbatim: bounds are defined by test
# inversion, and only the point estimate has a definition that outranks the
# port. This is the same class of decision as D-HEDGES (exact J over the
# hand-computation approximation) -- a defect there, because the approximate
# form is not the definition; a deliberate divergence here, because R's own
# artefact is not the definition either. Named so a future reader meets it
# as a decision with a reason, never as a discrepancy to diagnose.
